Rule 106: the English particle *forth* realizes the preverb `ἐξ-` and rides inside the compound verb's own unit, headed on the word glossing the verbal root; the auxiliary rides along under rule 9. No expressed preposition stands to answer to the particle.

Rule 31's closing clause: this second article stands in front of a prepositional phrase and the ASV supplies no relative clause for it to carry, writing only *to God-ward*, so it realizes nothing.
The ASV wraps the phrase in the discontinuous frame *to … ward*, permitted by rule 15; a proper preposition carrying such a wrap heads on the prepositional word under rule 78.
Rule 23: the ASV writes no determiner inside *to God-ward*.
Noun to noun.

Rule 106: *forth* realizes the preverb `ἐκ-` and stays inside the verb's own unit, no expressed preposition standing to answer to it; headed on the verb word, with the copula riding along under rule 9.
Rule 40: the conjunction takes the whole English clause-introducer *so that*, headed on *so*.
Rule 69: `τι` is rendered non-negatively as *anything* and cannot carry the negation, so the negator keeps the English negative word as its own aligned unit.

Rule 73: the light-verb pair `χρείαν ἔχειν` is collapsed by the ASV into the single English verb *need*, so the two tokens are one unit; the source head is the token the target head realizes, `χρεία`. Variant SBLGNT.1TH.1.8.v010 is underdetermined between r00-base and r01, both covering s031 and s032, so no textual decision is made here.
Accusative subject of the infinitive written as the English subject.
Rule 7: the infinitival marker belongs to its verb, no conjunction governing this clause.
Indefinite rendered non-negatively under rule 69.

review_notes: `χρείαν ἔχειν` is one unit under rule 73; splitting it would leave no English word for `ἔχω`.

`ἡ πρὸς τὸν θεόν` gives nothing to either article: the first because the ASV supplies no relative clause for it (rule 31's closing clause), the second because *God-ward* carries no determiner (rule 23).
Both compound verbs keep their *forth* inside their own unit under rule 106; no expressed `ἐκ` stands in either clause to claim it.
